exercises.summary: A staggered-stance hinge — most of the load on the front leg, but far easier to balance than a full single-leg RDL.
exercises.video_title: B Stance RDL Tutorial
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, then slide one foot back so its toe lines up with the other heel.
Put about 90% of your weight on the front leg; the back foot is a kickstand for balance.
Push your hips back and hinge forward with a flat back.
Feel the front hamstring stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
form_tips: The back leg only helps with balance — don't push through it.
Keep a fixed soft bend in the front knee.
Keep the movement in your hips, spine long.
common_mistakes: Splitting the weight evenly between both legs.
Rounding the lower back.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.summary: Curl your hips toward your ribs — a lower-ab move that spares the neck.
exercises.video_title: Reverse Crunch | Core & Ab Strength Exercise Tutorial
instructions: Lie on your back, hands by your sides, knees bent so thighs are vertical.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Use your abs to curl your hips and knees up toward your chest.
Lower slowly without letting the back arch.
form_tips: Small, controlled range — no swinging the legs.
Keep the lower back pinned down the whole time.
Exhale as you curl up.
common_mistakes: Using momentum to throw the legs.
Letting the lower back arch off the floor.
Pulling with the hip flexors instead of curling with the abs.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.summary: Raise straight legs to 90 degrees and lower with control — a lower-ab and core-control classic.
exercises.video_title: Leg Raises | Step by Step Tutorial | Proper Form and Technique
instructions: Lie on your back, hands tucked under your glutes, legs straight.
Press your lower back into the floor and keep it there.
Raise your legs together until they're vertical, then lower slowly.
Stop lowering before your back lifts off the floor.
form_tips: Bend the knees to regress; keep them straighter to progress.
Roll your pelvis under slightly at the top.
Lower only as far as your back stays flat.
common_mistakes: Lower back arching as the legs drop.
Using momentum to swing the legs up.
Yanking with the hip flexors.

exercises.name: V-Up
exercises.summary: Lift your torso and straight legs to meet in a V — a demanding full-range ab move.
exercises.video_title: V-Ups Tutorial For Beginners (4 Variations Covered)
instructions: Lie flat, arms extended past your head, legs straight, body long.
Exhale and lift your torso and legs at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet.
Balance briefly on your glutes, then lower everything with control.
form_tips: Bend the knees or do tuck-ups to regress.
Keep the movement smooth — no jack-knifing with momentum.
Keep your lower back from over-rounding at the top.
common_mistakes: Throwing the arms for momentum.
Crashing back down instead of lowering.
Bending the legs when you meant to keep them straight.

exercises.name: Hollow Rock
exercises.summary: Hold the hollow shape and rock — adds a dynamic challenge to the gymnastics core position.
exercises.video_title: How To: Hollow Rock
instructions: Get into a hollow hold: lower back pressed down, shoulders and legs a few inches off the floor.
Keeping the shape rigid, rock forward and back from your upper back to your hips.
Keep the rock small; hands and feet never touch the floor.
form_tips: The lower back stays glued down the whole time.
Rock from the shape, not by breaking at the hips.
Master the static hollow hold first.
common_mistakes: Lower back popping off the floor.
Bending at the hips to create the rock.
Big, uncontrolled rocking.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.summary: A plank where you tap each shoulder — the anti-rotation demand goes way up.
exercises.video_title: How to Do Plank Shoulder Taps | Core Stability Exercise
instructions: Set up in a tall plank, hands under shoulders, feet about shoulder-width for stability.
Shift your weight slightly and lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder.
Return it and repeat on the other side, keeping your hips still.
form_tips: Widen your feet to make it easier, narrow them to make it harder.
Squeeze your glutes so the hips don't rock.
Slow taps — the stillness is the exercise.
common_mistakes: Hips swaying side to side.
Rushing the taps.
Piking the hips up.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
exercises.summary: Alternating elbow-to-knee with a pedalling motion — hits the obliques hard.
exercises.video_title: Bicycle Crunch Tutorial
instructions: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind your head, legs lifted, knees bent 90 degrees.
Bring one knee toward your chest as you rotate the opposite elbow toward it.
Switch sides in a smooth pedalling motion, extending the other leg out.
form_tips: Rotate from the ribs, not by yanking the neck.
Keep the movement controlled — quality over speed.
The extended leg stays off the floor.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the head and straining the neck.
Racing through reps with no rotation.
Letting the lower back arch.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.summary: Sit back, lift your feet, and rotate side to side — a simple rotational core builder.
exercises.video_title: Russian Twist | Proper Form Tutorial for Rotational Core Strength
instructions: Sit with knees bent, lean back to about 45 degrees, keeping your back flat.
Lift your feet off the floor (or keep them down to regress).
Rotate your torso to touch the floor beside one hip, then the other.
form_tips: Rotate through the trunk, not just the arms.
Keep your chest up and back long — no rounding.
Slow and controlled beats fast and floppy.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back.
Only swinging the arms.
Going so fast the range disappears.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
exercises.summary: A side plank with the top leg on a bench — brutal, protective inner-thigh strength.
exercises.video_title: Copenhagen Plank | Proper Form Tutorial for Adductor Strength
instructions: Set up in a side plank with your top shin or ankle resting on a chair or bench.
Let the bottom leg hang under the bench.
Lift your hips so your body is one straight line, squeezing the top inner thigh.
Hold for time, then switch sides.
form_tips: Regress by resting the top knee (bent) on the bench instead of the ankle.
Keep your body in one line — no sagging or piking.
Start with short holds; this move gets sore fast.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging toward the floor.
Going straight to the long-lever (ankle) version.
Holding too long, too soon, and tweaking the groin.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.summary: The simplest calf builder — do them off a step for full range.
exercises.video_title: Standing Calf Raise Tutorial for Beginners
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on the edge of a step, heels hanging off.
Let your heels drop below the step for a stretch.
Press up onto your toes as high as you can and pause at the top.
Lower slowly back into the stretch.
form_tips: Full range: deep stretch, high squeeze.
Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Progress to one leg at a time when this feels easy.
common_mistakes: Tiny bouncy reps with no real range.
Rushing the lowering phase.
Rolling onto the outer edge of the foot.

exercises.name: Jumping Jacks
exercises.summary: The warm-up everyone knows — gets blood moving and joints ready in 30 seconds.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Jumping Jack | Proper Form & Technique | NASM
instructions: Start standing tall, feet together, arms at your sides.
Jump your feet out wide as you sweep your arms overhead.
Jump back to the start. Keep a steady, springy rhythm.
form_tips: Land softly through the balls of your feet.
Keep a slight bend in the knees.
Step-jacks (no jump) are a fine low-impact option.
common_mistakes: Landing hard and flat-footed.
Locking the knees.
Half-raising the arms.

exercises.name: High Knees
exercises.summary: Run in place driving your knees high — quick cardio and hip-flexor work.
exercises.video_title: High Knees - Step-by-Step Guide
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward hip height, then quickly switch, staying on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms in time with your legs.
form_tips: Stay tall — don't lean back as you lift the knees.
Land softly and quietly.
March the knees up slowly to regress.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to get the knees up.
Heavy, flat-footed landings.
Barely lifting the knees.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
exercises.summary: Jump and pull your knees to your chest — a high-intensity power and conditioning move.
exercises.video_title: Tuck Jumps – Power & Explosiveness
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, dip into a quarter squat.
Explode straight up and pull your knees toward your chest.
Land softly in a quarter squat and immediately reset.
form_tips: Land quiet with soft knees and hips.
Keep your chest up; don't fold forward to reach the knees.
Warm up thoroughly — this is high-impact.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged.
Piking the torso down to meet the knees.
Doing them fatigued, which wrecks the landing mechanics.

exercises.name: Inchworm Walkout
exercises.summary: Fold, walk your hands out to a plank, walk them back — a full-body warm-up and core drill.
exercises.video_title: Inchworm Walk Out
instructions: Stand tall, hinge forward and place your hands on the floor, legs as straight as comfortable.
Walk your hands forward until you're in a solid plank.
Optionally add a push-up, then walk your hands back to your feet and stand up.
form_tips: Actually put weight on your hands — no 'air walking'.
Keep your hips level in the plank, no sag.
Pause a beat in the fold and in the plank.
common_mistakes: Rushing and skipping the walk-back.
Hips sagging in the plank.
Bouncing up instead of a controlled stand.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise
exercises.summary: Raise the band out to the sides for wider shoulders — constant tension, joint-friendly.
exercises.video_title: How To: Resistance Band Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band, an end in each hand at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise your hands out to the sides, leading with the elbows, to about shoulder height.
Lower slowly with control.
form_tips: Keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Thumbs level with or slightly above the pinkies.
Stop at shoulder height — no higher.
common_mistakes: Shrugging so the traps take over.
Using body swing to start the rep.
Raising the arms above shoulder height.

exercises.name: Band Upright Row
exercises.summary: Pull the band up the front of your body — hits the side delts and upper traps.
exercises.video_title: Resistance Band Upright Row – Perfect Form Guide
instructions: Stand on the band, hands close together in front of your thighs.
Pull the band straight up the front of your body, leading with your elbows.
Stop when your hands reach chest height and your elbows are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly.
form_tips: Keep the band close to your body.
Elbows lead and stay higher than the wrists.
If your shoulders pinch, stop lower and widen the grip.
common_mistakes: Pulling the elbows above the shoulders (shoulder impingement risk).
Letting the band drift away from the body.
Using a jerky, momentum-driven pull.

exercises.name: Band Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.summary: Extend the band overhead to target the long head of the triceps.
exercises.video_title: Band Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Stand on the band, bring your hands behind your head with elbows pointing up.
Brace your core and keep your upper arms still.
Extend your elbows to press the band overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly behind your head.
form_tips: Elbows point at the ceiling and stay there.
Keep your ribs down — don't arch to press.
Keep constant tension; don't rest at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring forward.
Arching the lower back.
Only doing a partial range.

exercises.name: Band Triceps Kickback
exercises.summary: Hinge over and press the band straight back — constant tension right where the triceps lock out.
exercises.video_title: Triceps Kickback / Pushdown — Band Tutorial
instructions: Stand on the band and hinge your torso forward to about 45 degrees, flat back.
Tuck your upper arms against your sides, elbows bent 90 degrees.
Straighten your elbows to press the band back, squeezing the triceps.
Return slowly to 90 degrees.
form_tips: Upper arms stay pinned — only the forearms move.
Squeeze for a beat at full extension.
Keep a neutral spine; don't round the back.
common_mistakes: Upper arms drifting as you press.
Rounding the lower back.
Swinging the weight instead of controlling it.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.summary: One flowing move that opens the hips, hamstrings and upper back — the ideal pre-workout stretch.
exercises.video_title: World's Greatest Stretch | Tutorial
instructions: From a plank, step one foot up outside the same-side hand into a deep lunge.
Drop the back knee if you need to; keep a long spine.
Reach the inside hand's elbow toward your instep, then rotate that arm up to the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Return the hand down, step back to plank, and switch sides.
form_tips: Move slowly and breathe into each position.
Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.
Only rotate as far as feels open, not forced.
common_mistakes: Rushing through instead of holding each phase.
Rounding the back in the lunge.
Forcing the rotation.

exercises.name: Cat–Cow
exercises.summary: Slow spinal flexion and extension on all fours — wakes up the back before you load it.
exercises.video_title: Cat–Cow Stretch | Proper Form Tutorial for Spinal Mobility
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Inhale and drop your belly, lifting your chest and tailbone (cow).
Exhale and round your spine toward the ceiling, tucking your chin and tailbone (cat).
Flow slowly between the two with your breath.
form_tips: Let the movement travel the whole spine, not just the lower back.
Move with your breath — slow and smooth.
Keep your arms straight and shoulders away from your ears.
common_mistakes: Only moving the lower back.
Rushing the reps.
Sagging into the shoulders in the 'cow' position.

exercises.name: Downward Dog
exercises.summary: An inverted-V stretch for the whole back line — hamstrings, calves and shoulders at once.
exercises.video_title: How to Do Downward Dog | Proper Form & Technique for Beginners
instructions: Start on all fours, hands slightly ahead of your shoulders.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back into an upside-down V.
Press the floor away, lengthen your spine, and let your heels sink toward the floor.
Bend the knees as much as you need to keep the back long.
form_tips: A long spine matters more than straight legs — bend the knees freely.
Spread your fingers and press through the whole hand.
Relax your neck; let your head hang.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to force the heels down.
Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears.
Putting all the weight in the wrists.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
exercises.summary: Sit in the bottom of a squat and breathe — restores the hip and ankle range squatting needs.
exercises.video_title: How to Deep Squat Hold
instructions: Stand with feet a little wider than shoulders, toes slightly out.
Sit all the way down into a squat, keeping your whole foot on the floor.
Use your elbows to gently press your knees out and lift your chest.
Hold, breathing slowly. Hold a support in front of you if you'd tip backward.
form_tips: Heels stay down — put a rolled towel under them if needed.
Start with 20–30 seconds and build toward a couple of minutes.
Relax into it; this is a rest position in much of the world.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the floor.
Rounding the back and collapsing forward.
Forcing depth your ankles can't give yet.

exercises.name: Thoracic Open Book
exercises.summary: A side-lying rotation that frees up the upper back — fixes the stiffness that wrecks overhead and rotation work.
exercises.video_title: How to Do T-Spine Rotation (Open Book) | Thoracic Mobility
instructions: Lie on your side, knees stacked and bent 90 degrees, arms stretched out in front, palms together.
Keeping the knees down, sweep the top arm up and over to the other side, following it with your eyes.
Let your chest open toward the ceiling, then return the arm slowly.
Finish reps, then switch sides.
form_tips: Keep the bottom knee pinned down — the rotation comes from the upper back.
Exhale as you open up.
Move slowly and pause at end range.
common_mistakes: Letting the knees lift and rolling the hips.
Forcing the arm down with momentum.
Holding your breath.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
exercises.summary: A pressing start point that protects the shoulder by limiting depth.
exercises.video_title: How To Do A Dumbbell Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor with knees bent and a dumbbell in each hand.
Press the weights up until the arms are straight over the chest.
Lower until the backs of the upper arms touch the floor, then press again.
form_tips: The floor stops you at a safe depth — let the triceps rest on it briefly.
Keep the wrists stacked directly over the elbows.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows to 90° — keep them nearer 45° from the body.
Bouncing the arms off the floor to start the next rep.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Incline Press
exercises.summary: Tilts the press toward the upper chest and shoulders.
exercises.video_title: How to do the INCLINE DUMBBELL BENCH PRESS! | 2 Minute Tutorial
instructions: Set a bench to about 30°, sit back with a dumbbell on each thigh.
Kick the weights up to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press until the arms are straight, then lower under control to chest level.
form_tips: 30–45° is enough — steeper turns it into a shoulder press.
Keep the shoulder blades pinned back against the bench.
common_mistakes: Setting the bench too upright and losing the chest entirely.
Clanging the dumbbells together at the top.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Neutral-Grip Press
exercises.summary: Palms-facing press — the friendliest option for cranky shoulders.
exercises.video_title: Neutral Grip DB Press for Maximum Chest & Tricep Gains
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Press straight up, keeping the elbows tucked close to the ribs.
Lower slowly until you feel a light stretch across the chest.
form_tips: The neutral grip keeps the shoulder in its happiest position.
Drive the feet into the floor for a stable base.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift wide, which defeats the purpose of the grip.
Bouncing at the bottom instead of controlling the stretch.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Flye
exercises.summary: An isolation move that trains the chest through a long stretch.
exercises.video_title: How To Properly Do Dumbbell Floor Flys  (No More Shoulder Pain)
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells pressed over the chest, palms facing.
With a soft, fixed elbow bend, open the arms out in a wide arc.
Stop when the upper arms are level with the torso, then hug them back together.
form_tips: Think about hugging a barrel, not pressing.
Go lighter than you expect — the leverage is brutal at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows, turning it into a bad press.
Dropping below shoulder level and straining the shoulder capsule.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.summary: Overhead pressing with back support so the spine can relax.
exercises.video_title: How to do the SEATED DUMBBELL SHOULDER PRESS! | 2 Minute Tutorial
instructions: Sit on an upright bench with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press overhead until the arms are straight but not locked hard.
Lower under control until the elbows are level with the shoulders.
form_tips: Keep the ribs down — do not arch the lower back to finish the rep.
Let the dumbbells drift slightly together as they rise.
common_mistakes: Pressing the weights forward instead of straight up.
Dropping the elbows far below shoulder height between reps.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.summary: A rotating overhead press that hits front and side delts together.
exercises.video_title: How to do the SEATED DUMBBELL ARNOLD PRESS! | 2 Minute Tutorial
instructions: Start seated with dumbbells at chest height, palms facing you.
Press up while rotating the palms to face forward.
Reverse the rotation exactly on the way down.
form_tips: Rotate smoothly through the whole press, not all at the top.
Use less weight than a straight shoulder press.
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation and letting the wrists twist under load.
Arching the back to grind out extra reps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Push Press
exercises.summary: A leg-assisted overhead press that trains full-body power.
exercises.video_title: Make your heavy dumbbell push press easier!
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at shoulder height, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches at the knees, then drive explosively through the legs.
Use that momentum to punch the weights overhead, then lower to the shoulders.
form_tips: The dip is short and sharp — a few inches, not a squat.
Legs and arms should feel like one continuous motion.
common_mistakes: Dipping so deep it becomes a squat-and-press.
Letting the weights crash back down onto the shoulders.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Flye
exercises.summary: Balances all the pressing and fixes rounded-shoulder posture.
exercises.video_title: How To Dumbbell Reverse Fly PROPERLY | MAXIMIZE REAR DELTS
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips until the torso is near parallel to the floor.
Let light dumbbells hang beneath the shoulders, palms facing.
Open the arms out to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades lightly.
form_tips: Think of pulling the arms apart rather than lifting the weights.
Keep the neck long — do not crane it upward.
common_mistakes: Using so much weight that the lats and traps take over.
Rounding the lower back in the hinge.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.summary: A two-arm row that builds the whole back and teaches bracing.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO: Dumbbell bent over row | #CrockFit
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a flat back, dumbbells hanging at arm's length.
Row both weights toward the lower ribs, elbows close to the body.
Lower under control until the arms are straight.
form_tips: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top of each rep.
Keep the neck in line with the spine.
common_mistakes: Standing up as you row, turning it into a shrug.
Rounding the lower back under load.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.summary: A row with the bench doing the bracing, so the back muscles do the rest.
exercises.video_title: Perfect Dumbbell Chest Supported Rows (KING of Back Exercises)
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench set to about 45°.
Let the dumbbells hang straight down from the shoulders.
Row them up toward the hips, then lower fully.
form_tips: Because the bench supports you, the lower back is spared entirely.
Pause for a beat at the top of every rep.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the bench to help the weight up.
Cutting the bottom of the rep short.

exercises.name: Tempo Goblet Squat
exercises.summary: A slow goblet squat that drills depth and control before load.
exercises.video_title: Goblet Squats: Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Hold one dumbbell vertically against the chest with both hands.
Squat down over three slow seconds, keeping the chest tall.
Pause one second at the bottom, then stand up normally.
form_tips: The weight at the chest acts as a counterbalance — it helps you sit deeper.
Elbows track inside the knees at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Letting the chest collapse forward as you descend.
Rushing the lowering phase, which is the whole point here.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Squat
exercises.summary: Two dumbbells racked at the shoulders — heavier than a goblet squat.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Front Squat | Exercise Guide
instructions: Hold a dumbbell on each shoulder, elbows pointing forward.
Squat down until the thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the whole foot to stand.
form_tips: Keep the elbows high; dropping them pitches you forward.
Brace the core hard before each descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the weights slide off the shoulders as you fatigue.
Heels lifting at the bottom of the squat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.summary: One of the hardest leg exercises there is, and worth every rep.
exercises.video_title: How to do the BULGARIAN SPLIT SQUAT! | 2 Minute Tutorial
instructions: Stand a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of the rear foot on it.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Lower until the front thigh is parallel, then drive up through the front heel.
form_tips: Almost all the weight belongs on the front leg.
A longer stance targets the glute; shorter hits the quad.
common_mistakes: Pushing off the back foot to help.
Letting the front knee collapse inward.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.summary: Stepping backwards is far kinder to the knees than stepping forward.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Reverse Lunges | How To | Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Hold dumbbells at your sides, feet hip-width.
Step one foot straight back and lower the back knee toward the floor.
Push through the front heel to return to standing.
form_tips: Stepping back lets you control the load onto the front leg.
Keep most of the weight in the front foot throughout.
common_mistakes: Leaning forward over the front thigh.
Taking too short a step and jamming the front knee.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
exercises.summary: A hinge and a balance test in one — outstanding for hamstring strength.
exercises.video_title: The BEST Single-Leg RDL Tutorial (Romanian Deadlift)
instructions: Hold one dumbbell and stand on the opposite leg.
Hinge forward, letting the free leg rise behind you as a counterweight.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then stand tall.
form_tips: Hips stay square to the floor — do not let the free hip open up.
A slight bend in the standing knee is correct.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso open to reach lower.
Rounding the back instead of hinging at the hip.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.summary: The most direct glute builder you can load with a single dumbbell.
exercises.video_title: How to do Dumbbell Hip Thrust the correct way (Perfect Technique Tutorial)
instructions: Sit with the upper back against a bench and a dumbbell across the hips.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips until the torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top, then lower under control.
form_tips: Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down at lockout.
Shins should be roughly vertical at the top.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the lower back instead of finishing with the glutes.
Pushing through the toes rather than the heels.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Farmer's Carry
exercises.summary: Pick up something heavy and walk. Brutally effective, impossible to overthink.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform the Farmerâs Carry
instructions: Hold a heavy dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Stand tall with the shoulders back and ribs down.
Walk in a straight line with controlled steps for the prescribed distance or time.
form_tips: Grip hard and breathe shallowly but steadily.
Do not let the weights swing or bang against your legs.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to counterbalance the load.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.summary: A one-sided carry that forces the side of the core to resist tipping.
exercises.video_title: How To Perform The Suitcase Carry
instructions: Hold one heavy dumbbell in one hand only.
Stand perfectly upright — resist the pull to that side.
Walk for the prescribed distance, then swap hands.
form_tips: The whole point is not leaning; go lighter if you tilt.
Keep both shoulders level throughout.
common_mistakes: Leaning away from the weight to compensate.
Rushing the walk instead of controlling each step.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.summary: Curling from behind the body puts the biceps under a deep stretch.
exercises.video_title: Stop Screwing Up Incline Dumbbell Curls (PROPER FORM!)
instructions: Sit back on a bench inclined to about 60°, arms hanging straight down.
Curl both dumbbells up without letting the elbows drift forward.
Lower all the way until the arms are fully straight.
form_tips: The stretch at the bottom is the reason for this variation — use it.
Keep the upper arms still and behind the torso.
common_mistakes: Swinging the elbows forward to start the curl.
Stopping short of full extension at the bottom.

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps Extension
exercises.summary: Loads the triceps in the stretched position, where they grow best.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO: Overhead Triceps Extension (BEST EXERCISE FOR HUGE TRICEPS) || PERFECT FORM (POWERBOMB)
instructions: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the top end.
Keeping the elbows pointing forward, lower the weight behind the head.
Extend back to straight arms without letting the elbows flare.
form_tips: Elbows stay narrow and high throughout.
Control the lowering — this is where the work happens.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare out wide.
Going so deep the shoulders start to shrug up.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
exercises.summary: A lying triceps extension with dumbbells, gentler on the elbows than a bar.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Triceps Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on a bench with dumbbells pressed over the chest, palms facing.
Bend only at the elbows to lower the weights beside the ears.
Extend back to the start without moving the upper arms.
form_tips: The upper arms stay locked in place — only the forearms move.
A slight backward tilt of the upper arms increases the stretch.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a press by moving the shoulders.
Letting the elbows drift apart under fatigue.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.summary: Simple, heavy trap work for the top of the back.
exercises.video_title: How to PROPERLY Dumbbell Shrug (FIX THIS NOW!)
instructions: Stand tall with a heavy dumbbell in each hand.
Shrug the shoulders straight up toward the ears.
Hold for a beat, then lower fully.
form_tips: Straight up and down — rolling the shoulders adds nothing.
Pause at the top to make lighter weight feel heavier.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders backwards under heavy load.
Using the biceps to help lift the weight.

exercises.name: Renegade Row
exercises.summary: A plank and a row at once — the core work is the hard part.
exercises.video_title: Renegade Row Guide | Form Tips, Muscles Worked, and Variations
instructions: Start in a push-up position gripping a dumbbell in each hand.
Widen the feet for stability and brace hard.
Row one dumbbell to the ribs without letting the hips rotate, then swap.
form_tips: Hips stay dead level — that is the whole exercise.
Use hexagonal dumbbells if you have them; round ones roll.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips toward the rowing side.
Placing the feet too close together to stay stable.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Thruster
exercises.summary: A front squat straight into an overhead press — a full-body conditioner.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Thruster Tips
instructions: Hold dumbbells at the shoulders and squat to parallel.
Drive up explosively out of the squat.
Use that momentum to press the weights overhead in one motion.
form_tips: The squat and the press should feel like one continuous move.
Breathe at the top, never at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Pausing between the squat and the press and losing the drive.
Pressing forward instead of straight overhead.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
exercises.summary: An old-school move that opens the ribcage and hits the lats from a new angle.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Pullover: Chest or Back Exercise?
instructions: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over the chest with both hands.
Keeping a slight elbow bend, lower the weight back behind the head.
Pull it back over the chest using the lats.
form_tips: Stop lowering when the shoulders reach their comfortable limit.
Keep the ribs down rather than arching to reach further.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows to turn it into an extension.
Going far too heavy on a move with long leverage.

exercises.name: Barbell Box Squat
exercises.summary: A squat to a box that teaches consistent depth and builds confidence.
exercises.video_title: How to Box Squat PROPERLY!
instructions: Set a box or bench behind you at roughly parallel height.
Squat back until you sit lightly on the box.
Stand up without rocking or bouncing off it.
form_tips: Touch the box, do not collapse onto it.
The box gives every rep identical depth, which is ideal for learning.
common_mistakes: Dropping down and losing core tension on the box.
Rocking backwards to build momentum out of the bottom.

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.summary: Lifting a loaded bar off the floor. The whole posterior chain at once.
exercises.video_title: How to PROPERLY Deadlift for Growth (5 Easy Steps)
instructions: Stand with mid-foot under the bar, shins almost touching it.
Hinge down and grip just outside the legs, chest up and back flat.
Push the floor away and stand tall, finishing with the glutes.
form_tips: Take the slack out of the bar before you pull.
The bar should travel in a straight vertical line.
common_mistakes: Jerking the bar off the floor with a rounded back.
Hyperextending backwards at lockout.

exercises.name: Barbell Incline Press
exercises.summary: Tilts the bench press toward the upper chest.
exercises.video_title: How To: Incline Barbell Bench Press | 3 GOLDEN RULES! (MADE BETTER!)
instructions: Set the bench to roughly 30 degrees and grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower the bar to just below the collarbone.
Press back up over the upper chest.
form_tips: 30 degrees is plenty. Steeper becomes a shoulder press.
Keep the shoulder blades retracted against the bench.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the upper chest.
Lifting the hips off the bench to press more weight.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.summary: A row from a dead stop on the floor each rep. Pure back power.
exercises.video_title: How To Build a Thick Back With Perfect Rowing Technique (Pendlay Row/ Helms Row)
instructions: Set the torso parallel to the floor with the bar on the ground.
Explosively row the bar to the lower chest.
Return it all the way to the floor and reset before the next rep.
form_tips: Every rep starts from a dead stop. No bouncing.
The torso must not rise at all during the pull.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rise to help the bar up.
Failing to touch the floor between reps.

exercises.name: Good Morning
exercises.summary: A hinge with the bar on the back. Humbling and highly effective.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO DO THE GOOD MORNING EXERCISE: Build Your Glutes, Hamstrings And Squat With Perfect Technique
instructions: Set a light bar across the upper back as in a squat.
Push the hips back and hinge the torso toward parallel.
Drive the hips forward to return upright.
form_tips: Start far lighter than feels necessary.
Keep the back flat and the knees softly bent.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back at the bottom of the hinge.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees.

exercises.name: Front-Rack Barbell Lunge
exercises.summary: Lunging with the bar racked in front. A serious core and balance challenge.
exercises.video_title: The Front Rack Lunge
instructions: Rack the bar on the front delts with high elbows.
Step back into a lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
form_tips: Keep the elbows high or the bar will pull you forward.
Take a long step to keep the front shin vertical.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso pitch forward.
Stepping too short and stressing the front knee.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.summary: An angled press that suits shoulders which dislike vertical pressing.
exercises.video_title: Landmine Press for Shoulder health (DO THEM NOW)
instructions: Wedge one end of a barbell into a corner or landmine holder.
Hold the free end at shoulder height with one hand.
Press up and slightly forward along the arc, then lower.
form_tips: The arc sits between a bench press and an overhead press.
Brace the core to stop the torso twisting.
common_mistakes: Twisting the whole body to push the weight.
Letting the elbow flare wide at the bottom.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.summary: Heavy, direct trap work.
exercises.video_title: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Hold the bar at arm's length in front of the thighs.
Shrug the shoulders straight up as high as possible.
Pause, then lower fully to a full stretch.
form_tips: Use straps if grip fails before the traps do.
Pure vertical movement. No rolling.
common_mistakes: Bending the arms to help the lift.
Bouncing the weight with the knees.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.summary: The simplest way to load the biceps heavily.
exercises.video_title: How to Do a Barbell Curl | Arm Workout
instructions: Stand holding the bar at shoulder width, palms up.
Curl to shoulder height keeping the elbows at your sides.
Lower under control to fully straight arms.
form_tips: Keep the elbows still. They are a hinge, not a lever.
An EZ bar is kinder if your wrists complain.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso to start each rep.
Stopping short of full extension.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.summary: A bench press variation that makes the triceps the prime mover.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO: Close-Grip Bench Press (TRICEPS BUILDER) || PERFECT FORM
instructions: Grip the bar at roughly shoulder width, no narrower.
Lower to the lower chest keeping the elbows tucked close.
Press back up, focusing on locking out with the triceps.
form_tips: Shoulder-width is close enough. Narrower just hurts the wrists.
Elbows stay tight to the ribs throughout.
common_mistakes: Gripping so narrow the wrists bend painfully.
Letting the elbows flare out mid-press.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
exercises.summary: A deadlift starting from knee height, letting you overload the top half.
exercises.video_title: Rack Pulls | Lower Back | How-To Exercise Tutorial
instructions: Set the bar on rack pins at about knee height.
Grip it as for a deadlift with a flat back and braced core.
Drive the hips forward to lock out, then lower to the pins.
form_tips: The shortened range lets you handle more than a full deadlift.
Reset your brace between every rep.
common_mistakes: Yanking the bar and losing the flat back.
Leaning back excessively at lockout.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
exercises.summary: A one-handed swing that adds a heavy anti-rotation demand.
exercises.video_title: Basic Kettlebell instruction 9 - intro to single arm swing
instructions: Set up as for a two-hand swing but grip with one hand.
Hinge, hike and snap the hips as normal.
Resist the pull to rotate as the bell rises, then swap hands.
form_tips: Keep the shoulders square to the front throughout.
The free arm can mirror the working arm for balance.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso twist toward the working side.
Gripping so tight the forearm fails before the hips.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.summary: A slow, deliberate journey from lying to standing under load.
exercises.video_title: Primal Foundation | Kettlebell "Turkish" Get Up Instructional Breakdown
instructions: Lie on your back with one arm pressing the bell straight up.
Roll to the opposite elbow, then the hand, and bridge the hips up.
Sweep the leg through to a lunge and stand, then reverse every step.
form_tips: The eyes stay on the bell for most of the movement.
Learn it with a shoe balanced on the fist before adding weight.
common_mistakes: Rushing the transitions instead of owning each position.
Letting the pressing arm bend at any point.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Front-Rack Carry
exercises.summary: Carrying weight at the chest forces the whole trunk to stay braced.
exercises.video_title: Kettlebell Front Rack Carry
instructions: Clean one or two bells to the rack position at the chest.
Stand tall with the ribs down and elbows in.
Walk in a straight line for the prescribed distance.
form_tips: Breathe shallowly but do not hold your breath.
Keep the wrists straight, not bent back.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to support the front load.
Letting the elbows drift out and down.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Halo
exercises.summary: A shoulder mobility drill that doubles as a warm-up.
exercises.video_title: How to perform the Kettlebell Halo
instructions: Hold the bell upside down by the horns at chest height.
Circle it around the head, staying close to the skull.
Complete equal circles in both directions.
form_tips: Keep the ribs down. Do not arch as the bell passes behind.
Go slowly and stay close to the head.
common_mistakes: Using a bell far too heavy for a mobility drill.
Letting the lower back arch as the bell passes behind.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.summary: A loaded side bend that builds shoulder stability and hip mobility together.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform a Kettlebell Windmill | Nuffield Health
instructions: Press one bell overhead and turn the feet away from that arm.
Keeping the overhead arm locked, hinge sideways and reach the free hand down.
Stand back up while keeping the eyes on the bell.
form_tips: The overhead arm stays perfectly vertical throughout.
The movement is a hinge to the side, not a pure bend.
common_mistakes: Bending the overhead elbow.
Rounding the spine to reach the floor.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.summary: Floor to overhead in one explosive movement.
exercises.video_title: 3 EASY TIPS  to INSTANTLY improve your kettlebell snatch
instructions: Hike the bell back and snap the hips as in a swing.
As the bell rises, pull it in close and punch the hand through.
Finish with the arm locked overhead and the bell on the forearm.
form_tips: Punch through late so the bell does not flip onto the wrist.
Master the swing and clean before attempting this.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell arc wide and crash down onto the forearm.
Muscling it up with the shoulder instead of the hips.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Suitcase Deadlift
exercises.summary: A one-sided deadlift that teaches bracing against a tipping load.
exercises.video_title: Build Your Core Quickly - Kettlebell 56 Suitcase Deadlift
instructions: Stand with one bell beside the foot.
Hinge down with a flat back and grip it.
Stand tall without letting the torso tilt toward the bell.
form_tips: Both shoulders stay level for the entire rep.
Brace the opposite side of the core hard.
common_mistakes: Leaning sideways toward the weight.
Rounding the back to reach the handle.

exercises.name: Goblet Reverse Lunge
exercises.summary: A loaded reverse lunge with the bell held at the chest for balance.
exercises.video_title: How To Reverse Lunge
instructions: Hold the bell at the chest by the horns.
Step one foot back and lower the knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to return to standing.
form_tips: The front load helps you stay upright.
Keep most of the weight in the front foot.
common_mistakes: Letting the torso fold forward.
Taking too short a step backwards.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Pulldown
exercises.summary: A narrow, neutral-grip pulldown that emphasises the lower lats.
exercises.video_title: Close Grip Lat Pulldown | Proper Technique + Form Tips
instructions: Attach a V-handle and sit with the thighs secured.
Pull the handle to the sternum with the elbows tight to the body.
Return slowly to a full stretch overhead.
form_tips: The neutral grip is usually easier on the elbows.
Pause briefly at the chest on every rep.
common_mistakes: Rocking backwards to move more weight.
Shrugging the shoulders up at the top of the stretch.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.summary: A guided squat that lets you push the quads hard with no balance demand.
exercises.video_title: Hack Squat | Exercise Guide
instructions: Set the shoulders under the pads with the feet mid-platform.
Lower until the thighs are at least parallel.
Drive through the whole foot to press back up.
form_tips: The fixed path means you can safely train close to failure.
Keep the whole back flat against the pad.
common_mistakes: Letting the heels lift at the bottom.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.summary: Trains the hamstrings at the knee joint, which hinges alone cannot do.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Lying Leg Curl | How To | Proper Form & Technique
instructions: Lie face down with the pad against the lower calves.
Curl the heels toward the glutes as far as possible.
Lower slowly under full control.
form_tips: Keep the hips pressed into the bench throughout.
The lowering phase is where most of the growth happens.
common_mistakes: Lifting the hips to help curl the weight.
Using a range so short the hamstrings barely shorten.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
exercises.summary: Pressing on a fixed path, ideal for training close to failure alone.
exercises.video_title: INCLINE CHEST PRESS | Exercise Form Guide
instructions: Set the seat so the handles are level with the mid chest.
Press until the arms are straight without locking hard.
Return slowly until a light stretch is felt.
form_tips: Seat height is everything on this machine. Adjust it properly.
Keep the shoulder blades pulled back against the pad.
common_mistakes: Setting the handles too high, which turns it into a shoulder press.
Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end of the press.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.summary: Overhead pressing with the spine fully supported.
exercises.video_title: How to PROPERLY Shoulder Machine Press (LEARN FAST)
instructions: Set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
Press overhead until the arms are almost straight.
Lower under control to the starting position.
form_tips: The back support means no lower-back strain at all.
Do not slam into lockout.
common_mistakes: Starting with the handles far below the shoulders.
Arching away from the back pad.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.summary: Chest isolation on a fixed arc, safer than heavy dumbbell flyes.
exercises.video_title: The Chest PEC DEC FLY | Exercise Form Guide
instructions: Sit with the upper arms against the pads at chest height.
Bring the arms together in front of the chest.
Open slowly until a comfortable stretch is felt.
form_tips: Squeeze for a beat where the pads meet.
Stop opening when the chest is stretched, not strained.
common_mistakes: Opening so far that the shoulder capsule takes the load.
Using the hands to push rather than the upper arms.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.summary: The easiest way to train the rear delts with good form.
exercises.video_title: How to PROPERLY Reverse Pec Deck Fly (DO THIS)
instructions: Sit facing the pad with the arms forward at shoulder height.
Open the arms out and back in a wide arc.
Return slowly under control.
form_tips: Think about pulling the arms apart, not lifting the weight.
Keep a soft, fixed elbow bend.
common_mistakes: Using so much weight the traps take over.
Jerking at the end range of the movement.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up
exercises.summary: A real pull-up with an adjustable amount of help.
exercises.video_title: How To PROPERLY Use The Assisted Pull Up Machine (DO MORE PULL UPS)
instructions: Set the assistance weight and kneel or stand on the pad.
Pull until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to a full hang.
form_tips: Reduce the assistance a little every couple of weeks.
More assistance weight means an easier rep.
common_mistakes: Using so much assistance the lats barely work.
Bouncing out of the bottom of the hang.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.summary: Loaded calf work through a full range of motion.
exercises.video_title: Exercises with an Athletic Trainer: Standing Calf Raises
instructions: Set the shoulders under the pads with the balls of the feet on the platform.
Rise onto the toes as high as possible.
Lower the heels below the platform for a full stretch.
form_tips: Pause at both the top and the bottom of every rep.
The stretch at the bottom matters as much as the squeeze.
common_mistakes: Bouncing rapidly through a tiny range.
Bending the knees to help the movement.

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
exercises.summary: Loaded trunk flexion, which bodyweight crunches cannot easily provide.
exercises.video_title: Cable Crunches: The CORRECT Way To Do Them (Most People Are Wrong)
instructions: Sit with the chest against the pad and grip the handles.
Crunch forward by shortening the abs, not pulling with the arms.
Return slowly to the start.
form_tips: Curl the ribcage toward the pelvis rather than bending at the hips.
Exhale hard at the bottom of the crunch.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms and shoulders.
Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.summary: A squat on a fixed bar path, useful when training alone.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO SQUAT ON THE SMITH MACHINE 2026
instructions: Set the bar on the upper back and place the feet slightly forward.
Squat down until the thighs are parallel.
Drive up and re-rack by rotating the bar.
form_tips: The fixed path removes the balance demand entirely.
Feet slightly forward keeps the knees comfortable.
common_mistakes: Placing the feet directly under the bar, which strains the knees.
Forgetting to disengage the safety hooks before starting.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction
exercises.summary: Targets the side glutes, which stabilise the knee and hip when you run.
exercises.video_title: Foolproof Guide to Side Lying Hip Abduction
instructions: Sit with the pads against the outside of the knees.
Push the knees apart as far as comfortable.
Return slowly against the resistance.
form_tips: Leaning forward slightly biases the upper glute.
Pause for a beat at the widest point.
common_mistakes: Slamming the weight open and letting it snap back.
Using the arms to push the pads outward.

exercises.name: Machine Chest-Supported Row
exercises.summary: A rowing machine with a chest pad, removing the lower back entirely.
exercises.video_title: Machine Chest Supported Rows | FST-7 Tips
instructions: Set the chest against the pad and grip the handles.
Row back, driving the elbows past the ribs.
Return to a full stretch under control.
form_tips: Because the pad supports you, you can push these very hard.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the end of each rep.
common_mistakes: Pushing the chest off the pad to move more weight.
Cutting the stretch short at the front.

exercises.name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
exercises.summary: Constant-tension triceps work that is easy on the elbows.
exercises.video_title: HOW TO: Cable Triceps Pushdown || 3 Golden Rules (FOR GROWTH)
instructions: Set the cable high and grip a bar or rope.
Keeping the elbows pinned to the ribs, extend the arms fully.
Return under control to about 90 degrees at the elbow.
form_tips: The upper arms never move. Only the forearms.
Spread a rope apart at the bottom for a stronger contraction.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward and away from the body.
Leaning over the bar to press the weight down with bodyweight.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.summary: A lateral raise with tension at the bottom, where dumbbells have none.
exercises.video_title: How to Fix your Cable Lateral Raise | DB vs. CABLE
instructions: Stand side-on to a low pulley and grip the handle with the far hand.
Raise the arm out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly against the constant pull.
form_tips: The cable keeps tension through the whole range, unlike a dumbbell.
Lead with the elbow, not the hand.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body to start the rep.
Raising far above shoulder height.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Flye
exercises.summary: A flye with even tension from stretch to squeeze.
exercises.video_title: How to PROPERLY Cable Chest Fly (FIX THIS NOW!)
instructions: Set two pulleys at chest height and hold a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance with a soft elbow bend.
Bring the hands together in front of the chest, then open slowly.
form_tips: Cross the hands slightly at the end for a stronger contraction.
Change pulley height to bias upper or lower chest.
common_mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press.
Letting the hands drift behind the shoulders at the stretch.

exercises.name: Cable Pallof Press
exercises.summary: An anti-rotation press. The core works hardest by refusing to move.
exercises.video_title: Cable Pallof Press | Proper Form Tutorial for Core Stability
instructions: Stand side-on to a chest-height pulley and hold the handle at the sternum.
Press the handle straight out in front of you.
Resist the pull to twist, then return to the chest.
form_tips: The further you step from the machine, the harder it gets.
Brace before pressing, and breathe steadily throughout.
common_mistakes: Allowing the torso to rotate toward the machine.
Using the arms to fight the cable instead of the core.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.summary: Isolates the lats without the biceps taking over.
exercises.video_title: Straight Arm Pulldown
instructions: Stand facing a high pulley with a bar at arm's length.
Keeping the arms straight, pull the bar down to the thighs.
Return slowly overhead without shrugging.
form_tips: A slight forward hinge increases the range.
Feel the lats, not the triceps, doing the work.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows and turning it into a pushdown.
Using the whole body to drive the bar down.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
exercises.summary: Standing side-glute work with constant tension.
exercises.video_title: How To Do A STANDING CABLE HIP ABDUCTION | Exercise Demonstration Video and Guide
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and stand side-on.
Lift the outside leg out to the side without leaning.
Return slowly against the cable.
form_tips: Keep the torso upright. Do not lean away from the machine.
Hold the top position briefly on each rep.
common_mistakes: Swinging the leg with momentum.
Leaning the torso to fake extra range.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
exercises.summary: Direct glute work through hip extension.
exercises.video_title: How To Do Cable Kickbacks
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff and face the machine, holding on for balance.
Drive the working leg back and up, squeezing the glute.
Return under control without letting the weight touch down.
form_tips: Keep the movement at the hip, not the lower back.
A slight forward lean of the torso is fine and stable.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher.
Swinging the leg rather than driving it.

exercises.name: Cable Upright Row
exercises.summary: A vertical pull for the side delts and traps.
exercises.video_title: How To Fix The Upright Row: Avoid Shoulder Pain & Maximize Growth
instructions: Stand facing a low pulley holding a rope or bar.
Pull upward, leading with the elbows to chest height.
Lower under control.
form_tips: A wider grip and a lower finish is far kinder to the shoulders.
Stop pulling at chest height.
common_mistakes: Pulling the hands to the chin with a narrow grip.
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears at the top.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.summary: Loaded ab work that lets you progress beyond endless bodyweight reps.
exercises.video_title: Cable Crunches: The CORRECT Way To Do Them (Most People Are Wrong)
instructions: Kneel facing a high pulley holding a rope beside the head.
Crunch down by curling the ribs toward the pelvis.
Return slowly without letting the hips move.
form_tips: The hips stay fixed. Only the spine flexes.
Exhale fully at the bottom to shorten the abs completely.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hips instead of flexing the spine.
Pulling with the arms to move the weight.

exercises.name: Cable Single-Arm Row
exercises.summary: A one-sided row that lets each side work through its full range.
exercises.video_title: How To Do Single Arm Dumbbell Rows
instructions: Sit or stand facing a low or mid pulley with one handle.
Row the handle to the ribs, elbow tight to the body.
Let the arm travel fully forward and feel the lat stretch.
form_tips: Allow the shoulder to reach forward at the front of the rep.
Keep the torso square and still.
common_mistakes: Rotating the torso to help pull.
Cutting the forward stretch short.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.summary: Lift it overhead, throw it down as hard as you can. Deeply satisfying.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform the Med Ball Slam
instructions: Stand with the ball at your feet, feet shoulder-width.
Lift it overhead, extending fully through the hips.
Slam it into the floor as hard as possible and catch the bounce or pick it up.
form_tips: Use a non-bouncing slam ball if you have one.
Exhale sharply on the slam.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to pick the ball up between reps.
Slamming with the arms only instead of the whole body.

exercises.name: Rotational Wall Throw
exercises.summary: Explosive rotation against a wall. Power the core can actually express.
exercises.video_title: How To Do A STANDING MEDICINE BALL ROTATIONAL THROW AGAINST A WALL | Exercise Demonstration Video
instructions: Stand side-on to a solid wall, a couple of feet away, holding the ball at the hip.
Rotate explosively through the hips and throw the ball into the wall.
Catch the rebound and reset for the next rep.
form_tips: The power comes from the hips turning, not the arms.
Pivot the back foot fully on every throw.
common_mistakes: Throwing with the arms while the hips stay square.
Using a bouncy ball that rebounds unpredictably.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
exercises.summary: An explosive horizontal push. Pressing power without a heavy load.
exercises.video_title: How To Do a Medicine Ball Chest Pass
instructions: Stand facing a wall holding the ball at the chest.
Push it away explosively, extending the arms fully.
Catch the rebound at the chest and immediately repeat.
form_tips: Absorb the catch by letting the elbows bend.
Stand close enough that the rebound returns to your chest.
common_mistakes: Pushing slowly, which defeats the purpose entirely.
Standing too far back to catch the ball cleanly.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
exercises.summary: A seated rotation with load, for the sides of the trunk.
exercises.video_title: Chris Everingham - Medicine Ball - russian twist - ab and six pack
instructions: Sit with the knees bent and heels lightly on the floor, holding the ball.
Lean back to about 45 degrees and brace.
Rotate the ball from hip to hip, turning the shoulders with it.
form_tips: Turn the ribcage, not just the arms.
Lifting the feet makes it considerably harder.
common_mistakes: Moving only the arms while the torso stays still.
Rounding the lower back as you lean away.

exercises.name: Wall Ball
exercises.summary: A squat and a throw combined. One of the best conditioning tools there is.
exercises.video_title: The Wall Ball | Anatomical analysis
instructions: Hold the ball at the chest and squat to parallel facing a wall.
Drive up explosively and throw the ball to a high target.
Catch it on the way down and flow straight into the next squat.
form_tips: Let the catch pull you into the next squat.
Aim for a consistent spot on the wall each rep.
common_mistakes: Pausing between the squat and the throw.
Catching with locked arms instead of absorbing.

exercises.name: Med Ball Overhead Lunge
exercises.summary: Lunging with the ball locked overhead. Brutal on the core and shoulders.
exercises.video_title: Med ball jumping overhead slams
instructions: Press the ball overhead with the arms locked.
Step forward or backward into a lunge, keeping the ball still.
Drive back to standing without letting the arms drift.
form_tips: The arms must stay by the ears the whole time.
Go lighter than you think. Overhead is unforgiving.
common_mistakes: Letting the ball drift forward in front of the head.
Arching the lower back to keep the ball up.

exercises.name: Med Ball V-Sit Hold
exercises.summary: A loaded hollow position. Simple to describe, very hard to hold.
exercises.video_title: Medicine Ball V Sit with Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit balanced on the tailbone with the legs raised and knees bent.
Hold the ball out in front of the chest.
Keep the lower back rounded and hold for the prescribed time.
form_tips: Lower the legs to make it harder, raise them to make it easier.
Breathe steadily. Do not hold your breath.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the hollow shape.
Resting the feet on the floor mid-hold.

exercises.name: Med Ball Dead Bug
exercises.summary: A dead bug with the ball pressed between opposite hand and knee.
exercises.video_title: Med Ball Core Workout à¥¤ Quadruped Bird Dog à¥¤ Heel Tap à¥¤ Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on your back and press the ball between one hand and the opposite knee.
Extend the free arm and free leg toward the floor.
Return to the start and repeat, then switch sides.
form_tips: Press the ball and knee together hard throughout.
The lower back stays flat on the floor at all times.
common_mistakes: Letting the back arch as the free limbs extend.
Rushing through the reps.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
exercises.summary: One of the best hamstring exercises requiring no machine at all.
exercises.video_title: Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl | Nuffield Health
instructions: Lie on your back with the heels on top of the ball.
Lift the hips into a bridge.
Curl the ball toward the glutes with the heels, then push it back out.
form_tips: Keep the hips high the entire time. Do not let them sag.
Straightening the legs slowly is the hardest part.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips drop as the ball rolls out.
Rushing so the ball wobbles out of control.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Rollout
exercises.summary: An anti-extension rollout with a friendlier learning curve than a wheel.
exercises.video_title: How to Do a Stability Ball Roll In
instructions: Kneel with the forearms on the ball.
Roll the ball forward, extending the body into a long line.
Pull it back using the abs, not the hips.
form_tips: Keep the ribs down and the glutes squeezed throughout.
Roll only as far as you can go without the back arching.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back sag at full extension.
Pulling back with the hips instead of the abs.

exercises.name: Stir the Pot
exercises.summary: A plank on the ball with slow circles. Deceptively brutal.
exercises.video_title: Stir the Pot Exercise - Behm Muscle & Joint Clinic
instructions: Set up in a plank with the forearms on the ball and feet wide.
Keeping the body rigid, draw small circles with the forearms.
Complete equal circles in both directions.
form_tips: The body must not move at all. Only the arms travel.
Start with tiny circles and grow them as you improve.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rock or rotate with the circles.
Making circles so large the form collapses.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Pike
exercises.summary: A push-up position pike that folds the body over the hips.
exercises.video_title: How to do Swiss Ball Pike Exercise - Abs Workout For Women
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the shins on top of the ball.
Keeping the legs straight, lift the hips toward the ceiling.
Roll the ball toward the hands, then lower back to a flat plank.
form_tips: Push the floor away with the hands to keep the shoulders stable.
Keep the legs straight for maximum difficulty.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees and turning it into a tuck.
Letting the shoulders collapse toward the ears.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Wall Squat
exercises.summary: The ball rolls down the wall with you, guiding a clean squat path.
exercises.video_title: How to do a Stability Ball Wall Squat Exercise: WE-Can Program
instructions: Place the ball between your lower back and a wall.
Walk the feet slightly forward and lean into the ball.
Squat until the thighs are parallel, then press back up.
form_tips: An excellent starting point if free squats feel unstable.
Keep the weight in the heels and mid-foot.
common_mistakes: Letting the knees travel far past the toes.
Coming up onto the toes at the bottom.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Back Extension
exercises.summary: Gentle, supported strengthening for the lower back.
exercises.video_title: How to Perform Back Extensions on Exercise Ball
instructions: Lie face down over the ball with the feet braced against a wall.
Let the torso curl over the ball, hands at the temples.
Extend the spine until the body forms a straight line, then lower.
form_tips: Stop at a straight line. There is no benefit to arching past it.
Move slowly and deliberately throughout.
common_mistakes: Hyperextending the spine at the top.
Using momentum to swing up.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Dumbbell Press
exercises.summary: A dumbbell press with the bench replaced by an unstable ball.
exercises.video_title: Dumbbell Chest Press on Stability Ball | Anatomical Analysis
instructions: Lie back with the upper back and head on the ball, hips lifted.
Hold dumbbells over the chest and press them up.
Lower under control, keeping the hips level throughout.
form_tips: The hips must stay up. Treat it as a glute bridge that also presses.
Go lighter than you would on a bench.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips sag between reps.
Using weights heavy enough to destabilise you.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Knee Tuck
exercises.summary: A plank with the feet on the ball, drawing the knees to the chest.
exercises.video_title: Stability Ball Knee Tuck: Instructional Video
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the shins on the ball.
Pull the knees toward the chest, rolling the ball forward.
Extend back to a long plank under control.
form_tips: Keep the shoulders stacked over the hands.
Do not let the hips pike upward as you tuck.
common_mistakes: Letting the lower back sag in the plank position.
Rushing so the ball skids out from under you.

programs.name: Foundation Reset
programs.subtitle: 4 weeks · 3 days/week · machines, dumbbells & bodyweight
programs.description: Your first month back. Everything here is guided or low-skill so you can focus on showing up, moving well, and leaving the gym feeling better than when you walked in — never wrecked. Three full-body days with a rest day between each. If life happens and you only get two in, that still counts.
programs.focus: Rebuild the movement patterns and the gym habit
weekly_progression: Week 1 — Movement week. Keep 2-3 reps in the tank on every set. Pick weights that feel almost too easy; you're re-teaching the patterns.
Week 2 — Add a little. Nudge weights up ~5% where last week felt smooth. Same reps, same easy finish.
Week 3 — Add one set to the two main lifts of each day. Push the last set to a comfortable ~2 reps in reserve.
Week 4 — Hold the weights, tighten the form, and enjoy that it feels lighter. Next stop: Full Body Basics.

slots.coach_note: Warm-up. Do these before every session.
Main lift. Chest tall, sit between your knees.

programs.name: Full Body Basics
programs.subtitle: 6 weeks · 3 days/week · barbell & dumbbell compounds
programs.description: Once the patterns feel natural, this is where strength comes back. Three full-body days built around the squat, hinge, press and row. You'll do the same lifts each week and add a small amount of weight — that steady, boring progress is exactly what works. Start lighter than your ego wants.
programs.focus: Learn the big lifts and add weight every week
weekly_progression: Week 1 — Find your working weights. Every set should end with 3 reps left in you. Film your top set of the squat and hinge.
Week 2 — Add ~2.5-5 kg (5-10 lb) to the big lifts, or 1-2 reps to the accessories.
Week 3 — Add weight again where form held. If a lift stalled, repeat last week's number.
Week 4 — Lighter 'deload' feel: drop the main lifts to ~80% and focus on crisp technique. You've earned the easy week.
Week 5 — Back to adding weight. You should now be past your Week 1 numbers on everything.
Week 6 — Push for a strong (but clean) top set on each main lift, then reassess. Comeback Strength is waiting.

programs.name: Comeback Strength
programs.subtitle: 6 weeks · 4 days/week · upper / lower split
programs.description: For when three days feels too few and the big lifts feel like old friends again. Two upper and two lower days let you train each area twice a week with enough volume to actually build muscle, while keeping any single session under an hour. Best started after a full run through Full Body Basics.
programs.focus: More volume, split across four focused days
weekly_progression: Week 1 — Re-establish working weights across all four days. Leave 2-3 reps in reserve everywhere.
Week 2 — Add weight or reps to the primary lift on each day.
Week 3 — Add a set to one accessory per day. Primary lifts: small weight bump.
Week 4 — Deload. Cut sets roughly in half and keep weights moderate.
Week 5 — Ramp back up, aiming to beat your Week 3 top sets.
Week 6 — Peak week: one hard top set per primary lift, then take a few easy days and reassess your goals.

programs.name: Foundation
programs.subtitle: 4 weeks · 3 days/week · bodyweight & bands only
programs.description: Your first month with nothing but a mat, a wall and a set of bands. Three full-body days, one exercise per movement pattern, every set stopping well short of failure. Week 1 should feel almost too easy — that's the point. Miss a day and the plan still works.

Week 2 — Add 2–3 reps per set where last week felt smooth.
Week 3 — Add one set to the first two moves of each day.
Week 4 — Hold everything steady, sharpen the form, then move up a step on any chain that feels easy. Next: Build.

programs.name: Build
programs.subtitle: 6 weeks · 4 days/week · upper / lower · bodyweight & bands
programs.description: Four focused days — two upper, two lower — with enough volume and intensity variety to actually build muscle from bands and bodyweight. Antagonist supersets keep sessions under 45 minutes. Week 4 is lighter on purpose. Falls back to 3 full-body days if that's all your week allows.
weekly_progression: Week 1 — Find your working chain steps. Every set ends with 2–3 reps left.
Week 2 — Add reps toward the top of each range, or a heavier band.
Week 3 — Add a set to one accessory per day; step up a chain rung where you own the range.
Week 4 — Deload: drop one set from every exercise, keep the reps easy.
Week 5 — Back to progressing; you should beat your Week 3 numbers.
Week 6 — Push a strong-but-clean top set on each first exercise, then reassess. Next: Peak.

pattern_blurbs.horizontal_push: Push-ups and band presses. Chest, shoulders, triceps.
pattern_blurbs.horizontal_pull: Rows. The counter to all that pressing — build a strong back.
pattern_blurbs.vertical_push: Overhead strength: band presses and pike push-ups.
pattern_blurbs.vertical_pull: Pulldowns. Bands keep the back balanced; a bar unlocks pull-ups.
pattern_blurbs.squat: Knee-dominant. Squat to split squat to pistol — a very high ceiling.
pattern_blurbs.hinge: Hip-dominant. Bridges, band pull-throughs, single-leg RDLs.
pattern_blurbs.lunge: Split-stance strength, balance and everyday power.
pattern_blurbs.core_anti_extension: Resist the spine arching: planks, dead bugs, hollow holds, leg raises.
pattern_blurbs.core_anti_rotation: Resist the torso twisting: bird dogs, plank taps, band Pallof press.
pattern_blurbs.core_anti_lateral: Resist tipping sideways: side planks and Copenhagen planks.
pattern_blurbs.core_rotation: Train the twist: bicycle crunches, Russian twists.
pattern_blurbs.conditioning: Short bursts to finish a session and build your engine.
pattern_blurbs.mobility: Loosen up before you lift — hips, spine, shoulders, ankles.
